title: Jalen Carter signs record $152m extension with Eagles
description: Jalen Carter has signed a four-year extension with the Philadelphia Eagles, the club said Tuesday, in a deal that reportedly makes him the highest-paid defensive tackle in NFL history.Carter has 13.5 quarterback sacks and 108 tackles across his first three seasons with Philadelphia.
fullText:
Jalen Carter has signed a four-year extension with the Philadelphia Eagles, the club said Tuesday, in a deal that reportedly makes him the highest-paid defensive tackle in NFL history.

Though the 2025 Super Bowl winners did not disclose financial terms, US media said the extension was worth $152 million (133.5 million euros), or $38 million per year, with $106 million guaranteed.

Carter, 25, is one of the NFL's most highly-rated young defenders, having been selected to each of the last two Pro Bowls.

He was drafted ninth in the first round in 2023, and became a cornerstone of the Eagles' vaunted defense.

Carter has 13.5 quarterback sacks and 108 tackles across his first three seasons with Philadelphia.

His initial four-year deal had already been extended by one year, but the new contract locks down his long-term future.

"He disrupts the game, he's smart, and he plays hard," Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio said in a statement.

"There aren't many like him out there and I'm glad he's on our side."

The talented star has also drawn controversy.

Carter was ejected from last year's NFL season-opener before playing a snap for spitting on Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott.

Just weeks before his 2023 draft, Carter was charged with reckless driving and racing, after a University of Georgia teammate and staff member in a different vehicle were killed in a late-night street race.

Carter, who was not under the influence of alcohol or drugs, pleaded no contest to two misdemeanor charges and did not receive jail time.

title: Draymond Green contract details: Why Warriors star is returning to Golden State on one-year deal
description: Draymond Green is officially returning for a 15th season with the Warriors.
fullText:
Draymond Green contract details: Why Warriors star is returning to Golden State on one-year deal originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

When the Warriors were eliminated in April, there was some thought this could be a major offseason of change in the Bay Area.

From Steve Kerr's uncertain future to the possibility of landing LeBron James, anything appeared to be on the table after missing the playoffs.

Months later, the band is largely back together for Golden State. The final major piece of the puzzle fell into place on Tuesday, with Draymond Green inking a new deal to return for a 15th season with the Warriors.

Here are the details on Green's new contract.

SN's NBA HQ: Live NBA scores | Updated NBA standings | Full NBA schedule

Green has agreed to a one-year, $27.7 million deal to return to the Warriors, ESPN's Shams Charania reports.

That's the exact deal Green opted out of in June, aiming to give the team some flexibility with a James pursuit on their mind. Before it became clear the Warriors wanted to pursue James, Green was reportedly expected to opt into the final year of his deal.

Green averaged 8.4 points, 5.5 rebounds and 5.5 assists per game with the Warriors last season and is the NBA's second-longest tenured player with one team behind only Curry.

title: How the Jets have built a better defense than the NFL realizes
description: Breaking down the improvements in the Jets defense ahead of the 2026 NFL season.
fullText:
The New York Jets have understandably received attention for the changes they've made on offense during the 2026 NFL offseason, but their most impressive work may have come on the other side of the football.

General manager Darren Mougey and head coach Aaron Glenn didn't simply add recognizable names. They built a defense with a clear philosophy in mind.

Every level of the unit now features a blend of proven veterans, ascending young players, and developmental prospects capable of competing for meaningful roles. It's a strategy that has largely flown under the radar. The Jets attacked the defensive front with both proven production and developmental upside.

Veterans such as David Onyemata, T'Vondre Sweat, Kingsley Enagbare, and Joseph Ossai give New York additional experience, physicality, and pass-rushing versatility. Their arrivals should lessen the burden on returning starters while creating healthy competition throughout training camp.

The front office also invested in the future through the 2026 draft. Rookie edge rusher David Bailey brings intriguing pass-rush potential, while defensive tackle Darrell Jackson Jr. adds another young body capable of developing along the interior defensive line. The second level received similar attention.

Linebacker Demario Davis gives the Jets one of the league's most respected defensive leaders, while undrafted rookies Jaden Keller, Chase Wilson, and Nathan Voorhis provide developmental depth that will compete for roster spots and special teams responsibilities throughout the summer. The secondary may be where the transformation is most noticeable.

Acquiring Minkah Fitzpatrick immediately changes the complexion of the defense. His experience, versatility, and playmaking ability provide Glenn with another proven veteran capable of impacting games in multiple ways. Cornerback Nahshon Wright adds size and depth, while rookie D'Angelo Ponds injects youth and athleticism into an already competitive defensive backfield. Rookie safety VJ Payne further strengthens the group's long-term outlook.

One of the most overlooked aspects of New York's offseason is that these additions weren't made simply to fill vacancies. They were made to create competition. Successful defenses rarely rely on 11 starters alone. They survive injuries, adapt to weekly matchups, and sustain production because quality depth exists behind the first team.

The Jets appear to understand that reality.

Instead of chasing splash signings at one position, they distributed resources across the entire defense.

That's exactly the type of roster construction Glenn has emphasized throughout his coaching career.

Jets Wire will continue to provide updates throughout the 2026 NFL season.

title: Fifa’s shameful scheme to sell off World Cup is gravest existential threat to football yet - but will anyone stop it?
description: Fifa’s latest money-spinning wheeze, to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investment, has been met with horror. Now its member associations must make a stand against ‘football’s nuclear bomb’
fullText:
Fifa spent 1,403 words in a public statement seeking to rationalise their new plan to sell off stakes of the World Cup to private investment, but a few choice phrases are now ringing out elsewhere.

“Shocking.” “Football’s nuclear bomb.” “Worse than the Super League, and bigger than 115.” “The line in the sand.”

None of that is exaggerated because it ties together so many of the extremes that have been pushing, pulling and twisting football - let alone the world - for so long, potentially crystallising so much of what has been coming to dictate its future: what the game should be and what it’s becoming; how it repeatedly shows it has a social value that you can’t buy as so many involved try to financially exploit that; what people say in private and what gets done in public.

You can even roll that right up to the seemingly dry details of governance like how the people who are going to vote on this - the heads of the member associations - are in many cases directly paid by Fifa through positions and committees.

This is when all of that matters most. How are they going to vote?

And, maybe most pertinently given the direction of the sport for so long, where is the resistance going to come from? Uefa have talked a good game, with a statement that directly says this “crosses a line” and rightly asserts the World Cup’s is “not FIFA’s to sell” - but are they finally going to play a hand?

Is this long-running tension going to spill out into a war that football arguably needs? Is anyone going to look at the bigger picture and actually make a stand?

Because, and this really can’t be stressed enough, once you start selling the game off, there’s really no getting it back.

Typical of how football and the world are going, Fifa’s 1,403-word statement of course turned all of this rationale on its head. It’s of a piece with Gianni Infantino’s unhinged Sunday statement about criticism. This announcement was headlined “Fifa intends to expand football development funding to over USD 10 billion subject to approval by FIFA Member Associations”, so duly framed by ideas of redistribution and democracy.

Once again, a not-for-profit raising money, any money, was automatically elevated as if it’s a good thing without any further thought. The core reality was finally referenced a bit further down, as Fifa spoke of “carefully selecting long-term investors who will purchase minority, non-controlling interests” in the new Fifa Forward Enterprise programme. That is set to bring the creation of a new company being formed to run the primary competitions, where Fifa would own a majority stake, private investors would have 20-30% and then the 211 members a small stake totalling around 20%.

Except, “non-controlling” isn’t how such money tends to really work. In reality, that kind of money brings a lot of influence.

There are profound concerns here even beyond the core philosophical virtue that the World Cup only belongs to the countries of the world - and, by extension, its football communities - and that’s it. What do they think happens once you allow such interests in? There might be the short-term benefit of being able to point your own national association to newly flush cash reserves of up to $20m - but what next?

Clue: such interests don’t tend to have wider societal concerns; they don’t care for what doesn’t make money. As one source puts it, “the current stakeholders benefit but everyone loses out in the future”. Trickle-down economics don’t work here, as the last few decades of football have made emphatically clear. This is why Celtic or Ajax don’t win the Champions League any more. It’s why every other country suffers a talent drain to western Europe.

And what would now be directly incentivised - especially through the establishment of a company to run all of this - is the expansion of the Club World Cup and all of the ideas that serve existing wealth, both in the game and society. It shouldn’t be forgotten that Infantino was involved in Super League discussions, with the clubs at one point thinking they had Fifa’s blessing.

The global governing body have now already confirmed that Josh Kushner - brother of Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner - has been in talks about becoming the proposed lead investor.

Infantino’s long relationship with the US president suddenly takes on an even sharper perspective, especially among the mooted next steps for this. An excellent exclusive by Martyn Ziegler of the Times has already broached that Infantino would be lined up to run the company as a “commissioner” once his final presidential term expires in 2031. In other words, a lucrative post-presidency life.

When you stand back, this looks a lot like one man using his position - and the sport - for personal betterment. Or, as one senior insider put it, “only in Infantino’s world can things somehow get worse for the game every day”.

It should be what anyone who cares for the sport stands against, but will those with actual say really do that? Will they, as one other insider states, “put their bollocks on the line”?

Some who despise the idea have already marvelled at its realpolitik “genius”, likening it to the fait accompli of the Saudi Arabia 2034 “acclamation” in how everything already looks lined up. Every individual association would get a huge figure - or could sell off some of their share in the new company - so those in power right now are clearly incentivised to vote for it. And this in a world where only a fifth of member associations actually return audited accounts to show how the money is used.

It reminds us how broken the system is, how the reform that was supposed to take place after Infantino succeeded Sepp Blatter never happened. And in that structure, how is this actually going to be stopped when such a financially attractive package is taken to Congress for approval and there are no checks and balances?

It all speaks to this central long-running theme of the game being taken further and further away from those who have an actual emotional stake in it; a personal stake - right up to the ownership of clubs. Members of the Fifa Council insisted they only found out through the media, re-iterating how the body now works. The FA, chaired by Fifa vice-president Debbie Hewitt, were completely unaware of the proposal and it was not mentioned at Friday’s board meeting.

Many similar figures declared themselves shocked, appalled, disgusted. Except we’ve heard so much of this before. This, more than ever before, is a time to act. Could Uefa countries actually threaten to pull out… or will the individual countries just look at those financial figures?

The world should watch how everyone votes on this. Hiding behind the majority, and pointing to Fifa’s dismally dull politics, will no longer cut it. This is a decision with repercussions way beyond all of that.

This is what all of the politics, all the game’s long problems, were ultimately leading to. This is the line.

title: LeBron James, 76ers To Be Showcased 34 Times On National TV
description: That is the maximum number allocated across Disney’s ABC/ESPN, NBCUniversal’s NBC Sports/Peacock, and Amazon’s Prime Video.
fullText:
LeBron James and the new-look Philadelphia 76ers will be showcased 34 times on national television during the 2026-27 NBA season, according to Front Office Sports.

That is the maximum number allocated across Disney’s ABC/ESPN, NBCUniversal’s NBC Sports/Peacock, and Amazon’s Prime Video.

NBA Commissioner Adam Silver said before the 41-year-old James dropped his latest decision last Friday that the league was waiting for James to release its schedule.

Among the highly anticipated matchups for the 76ers, who will feature a starting five of James, Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe, Jaylen Brown and Joel Embiid will be their games against the reigning NBA champion New York Knicks; Brown’s former team, the Boston Celtics; the new-look Miami Heat featuring Giannis Antetokounmpo; James’ first team, the Cleveland Cavaliers; James’ most recent team, the L.A. Lakers; and Steph Curry and the Golden State Warriors, a team James considered before choosing the Sixers.

"I would like him to make his announcement already, so we can finish the schedule, because, as you might imagine, the teams are calling us, the networks are calling us, and everybody wants to lock in the schedule," Silver said before James’ decision.

“But it will influence how we set the schedule, how we set opening week, Christmas Day, etc. So I need him to make a decision.”

In the wake of James’ latest move, the 76ers jumped to the third favorite behind the San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City Thunder to win the NBA title, ahead of the Knicks and 2024 NBA champion Celtics.

This article was originally published on Forbes.com

title: Tee Higgins goes viral for wildly funny moment at Kenwood Towne Centre
description: Tee Higgins received a new nickname from a woman outside Kenwood Towne Centre and it left him speechless.
fullText:
It appears Joe Burrow isn't the only Cincinnati Bengals player enjoying offseason fun.

Wide receiver Tee Higgins gave a glimpse into his offseason lifestyle with a self-care day vlog, posted on his YouTube channel July 27. The 12-minute video followed Higgins as he ventured through Greater Cincinnati, enjoying every stop, especially Kenwood Towne Centre.

As Higgins neared the mall's entrance, his final stop of the day, a woman approached him, saying, "Huh uh." Higgins embraced her for a hug, replying, "Huh uh? How you doing? You don't even know my name."

"Yes, I do! You fine chocolate thunder, you. I know exactly who you are," the woman said to Higgins, who appeared to be caught off guard. Higgins took a picture with the woman and chuckled to himself about the comment as he walked into the mall.

Higgins posted the moment to his TikTok account with the caption, "Nah, this was crazy."

It didn't take long for the video go viral, with over 200,000 views.

Of course, comments flooded the NFL star's video, with one user saying, "'Fine Chocolate Thunder from a stranger is so confidently insane."

"She's not lying, though," another person commented.

title: Leicester close in on Swansea's Wales forward Cullen
description: Leicester City head coach Russell Martin closing in on striker Liam Cullen from his former club Swansea City.
fullText:
Leicester City are in advanced talks to sign Swansea City forward Liam Cullen.

The Wales international played under current Foxes boss Russell Martin at the Swansea.com Stadium.

Cullen - who has won 15 caps and scored two international goals - has two years left to run on his contract with his boyhood club but is now expected to seal a permanent switch to League One Leicester.

Latest Swansea City news, analysis and fan views

Kilgetty-product Cullen joined the Swansea academy at the age of eight and made his senior debut in a 1-0 EFL Cup defeat by Crystal Palace under Graham Potter in August 2018.

He scored his first goal for the Swans in a dramatic 4-1 win over Reading on the final day of the protracted 2019-20 campaign, a result that saw Steve Cooper's men secure a Championship play-off spot.

Cullen has a record of 36 goals in 194 appearances across all competitions for Swansea.

The Swans are hoping to keep hold of last season's Championship top scorer Zan Vipotnik.

They also hope to use former Celtic striker Adam Idah more consistently following his injury-hit debut campaign.

Cullen's inability to be a regular starting number nine has often led the 27-year-old to feature in a deeper role, as he has done with Wales under Craig Bellamy.

Vitor Matos' side have already added wingers Elijah Just and Moussa Yeo - who can also operate in an attacking midfield role - to their ranks this summer, in addition to Stephen Welsh, Joseph Opoku and Leo Walta.

title: Lynx urged to trade for rookie sharpshooter to help Olivia Miles
description: Minnesota could use a perimeter shot maker to benefit from Miles' creation.
fullText:
Lynx urged to trade for rookie sharpshooter to help Olivia Miles originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Minnesota Lynx are already having a great season being led by rookie Olivia Miles.

There are rumors that Napheesa Collier could actually be moved before the upcoming WNBA trade deadline, but there are plenty of other options for the Lynx to consider, too.

One of them is a trade for more shooting.

USA Today's Mitchell Northam wrote in a new article on Tuesday that a logical target for the Lynx is Chicago Sky rookie Sydney Taylor.

Taylor was undrafted, but she's shining bright so far in her professional career.

"If there is an area where the Lynx could use a boost heading into the second half of the season it's guard depth and 3-point shooting," Northam writes. "Louisville product Taylor checks both boxes and has proven in her first full WNBA season she’s capable of playing in this league. Taylor is averaging 14.2 points a game, but perhaps more importantly for the Lynx, is shooting a solid 34% from 3-point land and ranks fifth in the WNBA in 3-pointers made per 40 minutes with 3.9."

On the one hand, it's fair to wonder why Chicago would trade Taylor at this point. She's been everything they could've hoped for and more.

There's a flip side, though, and that's this: The Sky have exceeded any value they could've hoped for from Taylor. By trading her now, they cash in on what she has become, rather than risking a decline that leaves them with nothing.

It would be fun for the Lynx if it worked out, because they'd have a sharpshooter alongside Miles for years to come.

It'll be worth watching, for sure, because if Taylor is on the block, a bunch of teams could be interested.

fullText:
Yet another blue-chip prospect is making the move to Bradenton, Fla.

After two years at New Jersey powerhouse Bergen Catholic, four-star EDGE Jackson Vaughn is transferring to IMG Academy for what’s now his senior season this fall. Vaughn reclassified up to the 2027 cycle this offseason.

The Notre Dame commit joins what’s easily the most notable high school football roster in the country. The Ascenders’ roster for this coming season will feature more than 30 ranked prospects, over half of whom are of the blue-chip variety.

$19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage

In 11 games for state champs Bergen Catholic last season, Vaughn racked up 40 total tackles, including 12 for loss and eight sacks. He was named a Sophomore All-American by Rivals.

He’ll make the IMG pass-rush look even more unstoppable alongside five-star EDGE Zyron Forstall, four-star defensive lineman Azhir Waddell, four-star DL Chase Foster II and three-star EDGE Andre Robinson, among others.

The Ascenders are loaded on both sides of the ball. Five-star quarterback Jayden Wade ranks as the No. 1 passer in the 2028 cycle; the senior four-star wide receiver duo of Eric McFarland and Osani Gayles is among the best in the country; four-star cornerback Aaryn Washington, four-star CB Censere Gaylord and junior four-star CB Phoenix Evans sit atop a deep secondary room.

Vaughn is the No. 148 overall prospect and No. 16 EDGE in the 2027 cycle, according to the Rivals Industry Ranking, a weighted average that utilizes all major recruiting media companies. He’s been committed to Notre Dame since May 26.

IMG is scheduled to open its season on Aug. 21 against Lone Peak (Utah). Per usual, it is playing a loaded slate filled with top programs from across the country.

The Ascenders went 10-0 last season and reigned atop the 2025 Florida High School Football Massey Rankings and No. 3 nationally, according to the Rivals National 2025 High School Football Composite Rankings. They begin this fall as the No. 10 team overall, per the Massey Ratings.

“Established in 1978, with a pioneering concept known as the Nick Bollettieri Tennis Academy, IMG Academy has since grown to become a global phenomenon. Today, IMG Academy is the world’s leading sports education brand, providing access and opportunity for student-athletes with an innovative suite of on-campus and online programming. IMG Academy is the only education brand directly responsible for filling one-quarter of all college roster spots on an annual basis. In 2021 alone, IMG Academy helped place 30,000 kids into college.”

title: Auburn football enters early race for 2028 five-star EDGE
description: Auburn football has become an early player for one of the top players in the 2028 recruiting cycle.
fullText:
Auburn football has entered a tight race alongside two Big Ten powers for one of the top defensive players from the 2028 recruiting cycle.

Chad Simmons of Rivals reports that Auburn has made a massive jump in the recruitment of five-star EDGE rusher Tyzon Swann. The recent move puts Auburn in a tight battle with Ohio State and Penn State for the talented Maryland pass rusher as the recruitment of 2028 players heats up.

Swann has visited Auburn twice, according to Simmons, despite being just a rising 11th grader. He tells Simmons that he values relationships, and that has been the driving force in Auburn's recruitment of Swann.

“Auburn is very family-oriented," Swann said. "They’re very helpful and caring people who want you to succeed no matter what.”

Swann is one of the 2028 recruiting cycle's top players. Already rated a five-star by Rivals Industry Rankings, Swann is the No. 1 player from Maryland and the No. 2 EDGE rusher from the class. According to the latest forecast from Rivals, Penn State is the favorite to land Swann with a 21% chance, followed by Ohio State at 13% and Auburn at 10%.

However, it is still very early in the 2028 recruiting cycle, and Auburn will have plenty of time to win him over and to expand its Maryland pipeline.

Auburn has zero commitments for its 2028 class, but is in a great position to ultimately land quality talent from the cycle, including in-state quarterback Sam Sollie.

title: Seven Ways to Make Your Email Aliases Even More Secure
description: Email aliases aren't foolproof, but these strategies can help.
fullText:
Email aliases were once a niche privacy trick. Now, though, they're a mainstream solution offered by any number of major email service providers, including Apple, DuckDuckGo, SimpleLogin, and Firefox.  Getting a basic alias set up and running to conceal your real email address is easier than ever—but given recent data leaks and sophisticated cyber attacks, it's increasingly clear that a basic setup only gets you so far.

That’s why cybersecurity experts now recommend having a nuanced email alias strategy that combines multiple aliases and secure authentication protocols to keep your real inbox away from prying eyes. As a journalist often working on sensitive topics involving security and compliance, I’ve been using email aliases for almost a decade. Here are some tips that have saved me a lot of privacy hassle over the years.

"Email aliases" refers to swapping your real email address with a stand-in that can forward emails to your primary inbox. That way, senders don't need to know your real email to communicate with you, and you can easily decommission aliases if they are targeted by too much spam.

Email aliases have been a standard practice for users who have to communicate sensitive information and maintain a degree of privacy, like journalists, lawyers, corporate executives, and public figures who expect to be targeted by spammers and cyber attackers. However, they don't replace real account security and won't stop anyone from breaking into your account if they somehow find your real email address.

Moreover, recent technological developments have made email aliases harder to maintain due to deliverability issues and data leaks. It's still fine to use email aliases to keep your inbox private, but you need an actual strategy to preserve your privacy now that spammers have grown much more sophisticated.

Email aliases hide your real address from the recipient, but not from your email provider or anyone determined to cross-reference your details from leaked data. So if you use the same alias everywhere or route every email to the same inbox without other safeguards, your email only looks private. Determined attackers can and will find ways to exploit that single point of failure.

Then there’s the other issue that no one warns you about. Most modern email services, including Gmail and Outlook, have built-in identity verification and will send shared alias domains straight into spam. If you want to get around this, not only do you need to set up your own custom domain for email aliases, but also properly configure your domain with authentication protocols like SPF and DKIM.

And finally, your email alias provider itself may be compromised, revealing your forwarding address through email headers, as in the case of Apple Mail. Alias providers may also have other points of failure, like the broken sync features in ProtonMail that many have complained about. So relying entirely on a single provider without a custom domain setup is a major red flag.

Clearly, you need to plan out your email aliasing strategy from the beginning to avoid missing important emails, being relegated to the spam folder, or leaking your private inbox through faulty technical implementation from your email service provider.

Most users prefer to maintain a bunch of aliases dedicated to different relationships, like one for personal emails, one for their work colleagues, one for scheduling meetings and appointments, one for streaming services, and so on. This works fine as a convenience hack to keep your inbox clutter-free, but it doesn’t insulate an alias if one of the services or applications associated with it experiences a data breach.

For example, if you had a single email alias that you relied on for all your banking and financial activity, Experian’s infamous 2015 data breach could have compromised all your financial services using that single vulnerability.

Privacy-conscious experts recommend maintaining a separate email alias for each service, such as one for Netflix and a completely different one for Apple TV, then bundling them under a single subdomain on your custom domain that’s specific to streaming services. That means your Netflix alias ends up looking something like [email protected]. So if one platform experiences a breach, your other aliases for similar services still remain private.

A common way to generate email aliases is to simply add a + sign next to your real email, such as [email protected]. This is fine for decluttering your inboxes, but doesn’t actually secure your email address because anyone can guess your real email address by removing everything after the + sign.

Instead, it’s better to use a combination of randomly generated words or hashkeys. If someone sees an email alias that reads [email protected], that doesn’t do anything to help them figure out the other email aliases on that same domain. This is especially useful if you aren’t using a custom domain yet and relying on a shared domain from your email provider or aliasing service, because those are even easier to guess.

Relying on your alias provider’s shared domain, like @simplelogin.io or @gmail.com, is problematic for at least a couple of reasons. For one, it makes it near-impossible to divest from that domain if you ever want to switch to a different email or alias provider. Whereas if you use a custom domain, you can just point that domain to your new aliasing service if the old one is no longer safe or convenient.

But aside from being locked into an email or alias service, you may also hurt your deliverability rates: A lot of these domains have poor spam scores that don’t pass most inbox filters. With a custom domain, you can set up your own domain authentication via SPF, DKIM, and DMARC. That way, inboxes assign you a separate spam score based on your own email activity, not the collective behavior of everyone else using that shared domain.

This is why a custom domain is a worthy investment if you want to keep using email aliases as a long-term privacy tactic. You have better ownership of your data and can set up business-level security features that aren’t available to free shared domain emails.

Here's what happened with people using the Hide My Email service in Apple Mail before July 7: Normally, Hide My Email generates a random two-word alias to conceal your real email from recipients, but due to a technical flaw, an attacker could easily uncover your real address by targeting your inbox with spam mail. They would simply spam your alias and wait for Apple Mail’s filters to respond back with a rejection notification, which would contain your real email address right there in the email header.

Whenever you receive an email forward from your aliasing service, expand the header section to make sure your real address isn’t revealed in the email metadata. (On Gmail, it’s the little dropdown next to the recipient name at the top of your mail.) If you see a "Forwarded-To" field with your real email in the message header, that means you have a leak.

Many providers bundle their email aliases with a password manager for easy access management, but that comes with its own risks.

Several users on the Privacy Guides forum note that they accidentally deleted all their SimpleLogin aliases when trying to clear the Proton Pass logins associated with those accounts. Apparently, Proton has an auto-sync feature connecting the two services that works both ways. It’s even worse if you’re not using a custom domain, because then those aliases are lost for good unless you can reacquire them.

You should regularly back up your list of email aliases in a text document or spreadsheet so that in case they end up getting deleted, you can create fresh ones with identical names and prevent important emails from bouncing off.

Many email providers retain records of your deleted account data for months or even years to comply with legal regulations. This makes them a common target for data brokers who scrape these accounts for any useful information. Luckily, there’s a simple fix.

When you’re about to delete an old email account or alias, make sure to replace any personal details associated with that account with random values before you shut it down. This includes your name, address, date of birth, and any associated payment details that could be used to single you out.

With many popular email providers like Gmail and Outlook cracking down on email aliases, you’ll often encounter a situation where using an alias to communicate is simply not feasible. Many inboxes have spam filters that bounce emails sent from random aliases or refuse to honor forwarding requests from your alias provider. It’s a compounding effect as well, because the more that email services reject emails from an alias, the worse it is for your alias’ reputation and deliverability rates.

For banking platforms, important package deliveries, legal communications, and other priority email messages, consider maintaining a direct inbox that does not hide behind an alias or rely on email forwarding to receive messages. This can serve as a fallback for situations where missing an email is just not an option.

title: 10 Shows Like 'Tell Me Lies' You Should Watch Next
description: More addictive shows about toxic relationships.
fullText:
A wildly toxic eight-year relationship doesn't sound like much fun—but better a fictional couple than me. The juicy, addictive Tell Me Lies (streaming on Hulu and Disney+) ended this year after three seasons, finally revealing the full story that unfolded behind the wedding that kicked off the very first episode. If you're seeking more salacious drama, here are 10 other shows that dig into similarly, uhm, complicated, messy relationships.

You want a toxic relationship? How about a string of them involving a hot serial killer? Penn Badgley plays Joe Goldberg, who, in the first season, develops an extreme romantic obsession with Elizabeth Lail's struggling MFA student Guinevere Beck. He'll do whatever it takes to clear a path to lasting love—like, literally anything. The show concluded after five seasons of toxic, obsessive relationships that were just about as addictive for audiences as they were for Joe. Stream You on Netflix.

These rich ladies are going through it, and just because they've got beautiful homes and nice clothes doesn't mean they're not getting the full treatment. As the series opens, five women (played by Nicole Kidman, Reese Witherspoon, Shailene Woodley, Laura Dern, and Zoë Kravitz) become involved in a murder investigation connected to a school fundraiser that threatens to bring all of their private dirt out into the open—and there are secrets aplenty to uncover. Toxic relationships come into the light, and others become toxic under pressure. In their social strata, any threat to the status quo can lead to big drama. Stream Big Little Lies on HBO Max.

Less overtly toxic than Tell Me Lies, this is nonetheless a show about a thoroughly complicated relationship over time, and no less compelling. This one comes from Sally Rooney's smart, bestselling novel about the steamy coming-of-age romance between Marianne (Daisy Edgar-Jones) and Connell (Paul Mescal), characters and actors with impressive chemistry. She's rich but lonely; he's popular but the son of a housekeeper. As time goes on and their roles start to shift, life and love only grow more complicated. The plot isn't groundbreaking, but its uncommon intelligence and a frankness about sex and sexual violence set it apart. Stream Normal People on Hulu.

A pitch-perfect (and pitch-dark) comedy, the Irish import Bad Sisters picked up several well-deserved Emmy nominations in its first year. Writer and co-creator Sharon Horgan leads the cast as Eva Garvey, oldest of five sisters, including Grace (Anne-Marie Duff), who's married to John Paul, an abusive and isolating husband. When the dude winds up dead under rather suspicious circumstances, down-on-his-luck insurance investigator Tom (Brian Gleeson) starts poking his nose into things. We know the sisters definitely wanted John Paul dead, but did they actually do the deed? Tom's family business will go under if he has to pay out on the life insurance policy, so he's motivated to pin the (potential) crime on at least one of the women. This isn't so much about a toxic romance as it is about toxic...well, everything. Stream Bad Sisters on Apple TV.

The title's affair impressively spins out over the course of five seasons via a clever, Rashōmon-like structure that has us constantly questioning our perspective as viewers. Starring Dominic West, Ruth Wilson, Maura Tierney, and Joshua Jackson, the show explores the extramarital relationship between West's Noah Solloway and Wilson's Alison Bailey, rotating between the points-of-view of the four leads to constantly put new light on events, while also suggesting that memories are ever-shifting and often self-aggrandizing. Stream The Affair on Paramount+ and Prime Video.

A messy relationship sits at the center of this addictive, if also slightly messy, South Korean miniseries. Art student Na-bi (Han So-hee) is coming off a borderline abusive relationship and no longer believes in love, which is not to say that she's entirely lost interest in sex. Convenient, then, that she meets flirty fellow student Jae-eon (Song Kang), similarly disinterested in anything long-term—at least initially. With impressive chemistry between the leads and a strong supporting cast of characters with their own issues, the show solidly depicts a modern situationship that slowly turns romantic despite its leads' best intentions. Stream Nevertheless on Netflix.

Sarah Shahi is Billie Connelly, a married mother of two in a quiet, wealthy suburb—and a woman with a rather wild past she's keen to reexamine. She starts daydreaming about her hot and horny relationship with an ex-boyfriend, Brad, writing down the sexy details, which her husband soon finds. And then it turns out that her bestie is sleeping with Brad, which puts her back in touch with the object of her fantasies. It's a show that asks: Do you stick with your safe, happy family or opt for the very extra good sex? Stream Sex/Life on Netflix.

Good luck finding a twisty relationship drama that goes harder than Behind Her Eyes, a show that builds to a climax so cuckoo bananas that you'll either applaud its audacity or cackle at its outrageousness. Louise (Simona Brown) is a single mother who starts an affair with her boss—and his wife—and then gets involved with his former mistress in the wake of a mysterious death. And then it gets really wild. Stream Behind Her Eyes on Netflix.

Based on your affection for Tell Me Lies, I'm guessing you're here for the drama—the truly fucked up relationships best enjoyed from the comfort of your living room (hey, no judgements!). In case you're looking for something a little less twisty and a little more sincere (and just as addictive), you might turn to Judy Blume. This adaptation of her widely banned 1975 novel updates the setting to current-ish day Los Angeles, and expands its exploration of the complexities of teen love and sex to include the challenges of being young, exceptional, and Black in 2020s America. Keisha Clark (Lovie Simone) attends a predominantly Black private school and is working toward a track scholarship at Howard, while Justin Edwards (Michael Cooper Jr.) goes to school with white kids and is on his parents' track to go to Northeastern, ideally on a basketball scholarship. Forever follows their budding romance in a way that feels real and compelling—it's one of the best young relationship dramas streaming. Stream Forever on Netflix.

A rom-com so dark and messy that it very nearly misses the cut-off for the genre, functioning simultaneously as a satire and a very believable relationship drama. Jimmy Shive-Overly (Chris Greer) is an entirely self-absorbed writer; Gretchen Cutler (Aya Cash) is a publicist/cynical chaos goblin. They have what feels like a one-night stand after a wedding, but find themselves drawn to each other, in large part because they're similarly self-sabotaging. Rather than a long will-they/won't-they build up, the two immediately dive into a wildly dysfunctional relationship; the question isn't "will they get together?" so much as "how can they possibly make this work?" Stream You're the Worst on Hulu.

title: Five Hacks Every Ultrahuman Ring User Should Know
description: More accurate data in workouts? Yes, please.
fullText:
Ultrahuman rings, including the new Ring Pro, come with an extensive app. Even before you activate any PowerPlugs (add-on features), there are plenty of graphs and numbers to get lost in. Here are a few hacks you should know to navigate the data deluge and make sure you're getting the most out of its clever hidden features.

I've used two of Ultrahuman's rings: the Ring Air, which I reviewed here (and which is no longer available in the U.S.), and the Ring Pro, which I wrote about a little here. Ultrahuman just came out with a new version of its app, so if anything here looks different from what you're used to (like the Longevity tab), make sure you have the latest version.

Ultrahuman gives you an estimate of your biological age, which you may (correctly) think of as kind of a silly gimmick—but don't ignore the longevity tab altogether. It's actually a great summary of your long-term trends. If you think of the Ring tab as giving your day-to-day data and suggestions for what to do today, then the Longevity tab tells you what all those days have added up to.

This is where you'll find an estimate of your VO2max, which gauges your cardio fitness. You'll also see a card describing your sleep debt; mine tells me I'm one hour in debt, due to bedtimes creeping later over the past week, but it also tells me a few on-time bedtimes should wipe out the debt.

Smart rings don't make great workout trackers, as I've told you before. You have to take the ring off for comfort or safety for many workout types, and the heart rate readings aren't particularly reliable, even when you may want to keep the ring on.

Ultrahuman can track workouts with the ring, of course, but the app also has a setting that accounts for exactly my complaints. If you have another device, like a Garmin or even a basic chest strap heart rate monitor, you can have Ultrahuman use that more reliable device for your heart rate during workouts. Just start a workout from the app (under the plus sign menu), and you can choose another device. It actually works with anything that can broadcast heart rate and gives you instructions for connecting your Airpods Pro 3, Apple Watch, Polar sensor, Whoop, or Garmin.

A new feature in the Emerald update is the ability to "train" your ring's heart rate detection algorithm. To use it, you'll wear a secondary device at the same time as your ring, and Ultrahuman will compare the signals it gets from the two devices. This is supposed to allow Ultrahuman to detect your heart rate more accurately.

So far, the feature is only available for a few specific Polar heart rate monitors, none of which I have on hand, so I haven't been able to test this yet. But Ultrahuman says that support for other devices, like Garmin, is coming soon. Training for step counting is also coming soon.

One of Ultrahuman's strengths is that it keeps track of the best time to do certain things. By default, you'll get recommendations about when you should stop looking at screens for the night, and you'll also get a recommendation to get a certain number of steps during the early morning and "golden hour" (around sunset) timeframes. There's a similar timeline for what Ultrahuman thinks are your best times to have caffeine during the day.

But there's another handy timeline you can add: one that shows you the timing for sunlight. To see it, go to Powerplugs and activate the Vitamin D plugin. You can use this for its original function, of course: taking note of when you are outdoors and getting sunlight. The ring detects some sunlight on its own, and you can tell it when you've been outside if you're trying to rack up a certain amount of time in the sun.

Now, you'll get a line on your timeline showing when the sun rises and when you'll get "partial sunlight" in the evening, customized to your location. You can infer some of this timing from the circadian windows plugin, but I like having it in its own little column on the timeline. I find this handy for planning outdoor activities toward the end of the day—if I go out near the "partial sunlight" time, I should probably bring a flashlight if I'll be on the trail. To see all your timelines in parallel, tap on the Active Windows card on the main screen.

One of Ultrahuman's most useful features is a simple battery-life setting that you won't find unless you go looking for it. When you first buy your ring, it will operate in Turbo Mode, which the app describes as running "all sensors at full intensity for continuous, all-day tracking." And sure, when the ring is new to you, maybe you'd like to use Turbo Mode and turn on live heart rate on the home screen so you can get the most data to look at.

But for everyday use, Chill Mode makes a lot more sense than turbo. This mode still tracks your sleep and restful periods, and it will still sample plenty of data during workouts, but it skips detailed tracking during other times. Your battery will last longer in Chill Mode, and honestly, I don't feel like I'm missing anything important.

title: Scammers Are Impersonating Spotify to Steal Your Credit Card Info
description: Those phishing emails are not from Spotify.
fullText:
Scammers love to impersonate trusted brands—ranging from big tech names like Microsoft and Google to password managers and payment apps—in their phishing campaigns to lure their marks, and their latest guise is Spotify. A new email is circulating alerting users to supposed payment issues, prompting them to hand over their credit card details and Spotify login credentials.

As The Guardian reports, Spotify users have received messages with the subject line "review billing info" claiming that the platform "encountered an issue while processing your recent payment." Recipients are urged to "review and update" their information to keep their accounts active. The button in the email directs users to a spoofed website, where users are prompted to enter their username and password, followed by their credit card number, address, and phone number—everything scammers need to make fraudulent purchases. One victim reported seeing a suspicious charge for more than $600 within minutes of handing over their information.

The emails closely replicate Spotify's branding, including its colors and logo, and appear to come from a sender called MySpotify. The fraudulent website also looks convincing at first glance. However, unlike some of the more sophisticated phishing schemes that exploit vulnerabilities in order to use real domains (like Google and PayPal), this one from Spotify breaks down when you look closer.

For one, both the sender's address and the website URL clearly are not connected to spotify.com or any legitimate subdomain. The subject line is all lowercase, and there are no specifics about users' subscriptions or accounts in the email body.

Payment issues are a common scam tactic, and you should always be skeptical of any communication that urges you to provide or update banking or credit card info (or sends you to a login page along the way, which is designed to harvest your credentials). If you receive a notification from Spotify about failed payments, don't click links, download attachments, or reply. Spotify won't request payment info, passwords, or other sensitive information over email.

If you're concerned about a payment or subscription problem, go directly to your account in the Spotify app or a web browser instead. If you've already entered your Spotify credentials into a suspicious site, change your password and keep an eye on your credit card transactions to catch any fraudulent charges. You can also forward phishing emails to [email protected].

title: Motherwell told to 'eat barbed wire' before Faroes test
description: Motherwell boss Alfred Johansson is bracing himself for a tough HB Torshavn welcome in Thursday's Conference League qualifier.
fullText:
Motherwell's players have been told to "go home and eat some barbed wire" as manager Alfred Johansson prepares for a demanding decider away to HB Torshavn on Thursday (18:00 BST).

The Fir Park side fly to the Faroe Islands carrying a 2-0 lead from a commanding Conference League second qualifying round first-leg victory last week.

Johansson's team dominated the ball and the statistics but, against a team who have not lost at home in European competitions for five years, the Swede is preaching caution as he eyes a place in the third round.

"We're going to try have a good performance," said the Motherwell boss.

"You have to respect the team that we're going to play and you're going to have to respect the place where we're going to play.

"In 10 years, I believe they've lost twice at home in European qualification.

"The last five years, they lost zero times at home, in European qualification, and that includes Brondby, which is a big club in Denmark. It includes Maccabi Haifa. It includes Helsinki. So these are pretty big, big clubs.

"And to think that you're just going to go there and grab a victory real simple, then you fool yourself.

"So I told the guys today 'go home and eat some barbed wire' and prepare for the battle because it's going to be a battle and you're going to have to be strong and brave to play our way.

"But the intensity is going to have to be there. Otherwise, there's no need to travel."

Elliot Watt, Elijah Just and Calum Ward have all departed Fir Park this summer, triggering a huge influx in funds for the fan-owned club, while captain Paul McGinn and stalwart Stephen O'Donnell remain sidelined.

A glut of young academy players flooded the squad in the first leg and flourished when given the chance, but Well fans will be delighted last season's Scottish Premiership top scorer, Tawanda Maswanhise, is set for a return.

The Zimbabwe forward has been out after sustaining a jaw injury in pre-season, but has done enough to be in the squad flying to the Faroes.

"Hopefully, it is looking quite good for JT at this point," Johansson said of Maswanhise.

"He will not start the game and he will wear protection. It is massive to have him back in, what a player.

"Did you see last season? What a player and it is a massive boost for everyone."

title: Korda & Hull seek major glory - Women's Open tee times
description: A full list of the tee times for the first and second rounds of the 50th Women's Open at Royal Lytham.
fullText:
England's Charley Hull will begin her latest attempt to win her first major title when she tees off in a prestigous grouping in the 50th Women's Open Championship on Thursday morning.

The 30-year-old has five runners-up finishes in golf's biggest events, including in June at the US Open, and will play her opening two rounds alongside Brooke Henderson of Canada and Australian Hannah Green (13:26 BST).

Hull's compatriot Lottie Woad will play with Andrea Lee from America and Japan's Akie Iwai in the opening two rounds at at Royal Lytham & St Anne's, with the group starting at 08:31 on Thursday.

World number one Nelly Korda of the United States and Korea's Ryu Haeran play alongside New Zealand's Lydia Ko - who pipped Korda to the Women's Open title in 2024 - in the following group (08:42).

Korda and Ryu have both won two majors in 2026 and have the chance to become only the fifth woman in history to claim three in a calendar year.

Korda can also claim the career Grand Slam with victory at Lytham because the LPGA recognises a player as having achieved the feat by winning four of the five major titles.

She has won three - the Women's PGA, the Chevron Championship and the US Open - and needs either the Evian Championship or the Women's Open for the slam.

England's Georgia Hall won her sole major title the last time the Women's Open was held at Royal Lytham in 2018.

The Bournemouth golfer, who has only just returned to tour life after the birth of her first child earlier this year, will tee off at 12:42 in the same group as 2019 Women's Open champion Hinako Shibuno.

title: Scarlets sign Wales fly-half Anscombe from Bayonne
description: Fly-half Gareth Anscombe signs for a third Welsh club after joining Scarlets from Bayonne for the 2026-27 United Rugby Championship season.
fullText:
Fly-half Gareth Anscombe has returned to Wales after signing for Scarlets for the 2026-27 season.

The 35-year-old former Cardiff and Ospreys player has joined the Llanelli side after spending the last campaign in France with Bayonne.

Scarlets have brought in Anscombe, who can also play full-back, to provide competition for Wales playmaker Sam Costelow.

"He's coming here hungry to compete," said director of rugby Nigel Davies about the 42-times capped Anscombe.

"He's joining Scarlets to challenge for the jersey and because he believes he can make a real contribution to this team - and that's exactly the type of mentality we want within our environment."

Scarlets have not revealed the length of Anscombe's deal but he will provide an experienced option after the region's struggles at 10 when Costelow was injured.

Wales centre Joe Hawkins had to deputise at fly-half - starting there 11 times last season - and Wales Under-20s international Carwyn Leggatt-Jones featured alongside his studies at Llandovery College.

Scarlets sign WRU deal but peace is temporary

Halfpenny commits coaching future to Cardiff

Welsh rugby's ins, outs and re-signings for 2026-27

Anscombe was limited to just five appearances for Bayonne in the Top 14 because of injury but believes he can make an impact in west Wales.

"I still have a huge desire to compete and to contribute on the field and help the team win matches," he said.

"Competition brings the best out of players and that's exactly what I want.

"My goal is to help push standards, share some of my experience and continue challenging myself."

Anscombe started his career in his native New Zealand before moving to Cardiff in 2014.

He made his Wales debut - qualifying through his Welsh mother - a year later and won the last of his 42 caps against England in the 2025 Six Nations.

Anscombe moved to Ospreys in 2019 and spent four seasons with the club before moving to Gloucester and then Bayonne.

Scarlets finished 14th in the United Rugby Championship last season, above just Dragons and Zebre.

They have bolstered their squad for the coming campaign with Wales prop Corey Domachowski, once-capped New Zealand forward Cullen Grace, locks Harvey Cuckson, Alex Groves and Tom Allen, hookers John McKee and George Roberts and full-back Isaac Murray-Macgregor.

title: Why can't Draper play & why won't surgery help?
description: BBC Sport's Ask Me Anything team explains the injury which has derailed former British number one Jack Draper's career over the past year.
fullText:
Former British number one Draper withdrew from a planned comeback in Washington on Monday after feeling more discomfort from bone bruising in his serving arm.

It is a similar situation to what happened at Wimbledon last month, where the 24-year-old Englishman also spoke positively about his fitness - and seemingly practised well - before pulling out on the eve of the tournament.

Draper continues to insist "finding acceptance and being patient" remains the key - but his fans can be forgiven for fearing the worst.

So what is bone bruising in the arm, how does it affect tennis players and would surgery solve Draper's long-standing issue?

Draper has been hampered by the bone bruising in his left arm for more than a year, playing just 14 matches in the past 12 months and missing all three Grand Slam tournaments so far this year.

He has dropped to the cusp of the world's top 150 as a result and will need to come through qualifying - or be given a wildcard - to play at the upcoming US Open, which starts on 30 August.

Bone bruising is essentially internal bleeding in the centre of the humerus bone, according to Prof Amar Rangan, vice-president of the British Orthopaedic Association.

The humerus is the long, tube-like bone between the shoulder and elbow joints, with the stronger outer layer - known as the cortical bone - protecting a spongier tissue called trabecular bone.

When the trabeculae break, the bleeding increases pressure inside the bone - causing bruising.

Tennis players are particularly liable to this injury because of the stresses imposed on the humerus by the rapid acceleration and deacceleration of their shots - particularly the serve.

Generally it tends to cause a dull, deep-seated pain, as well as limited mobility and inflammation for some people.

"How do you recover from this injury? A lot of patience - basically that is it," Prof Rangan told BBC Sport.

"It is almost a race between the bone healing and further stresses."

However, the notion of a player potentially needing surgery to fix the issue is emphatically rejected by Prof Rangan.

"The only thing can heal it is rest. The body has to heal and strengthen the bone," he said.

"Surgery would be further injury to the area and would not help.

"As long as there is sufficient relative rest to allow the bone to heal and strengthen and consolidate it should settle down."

Draper has leaned on other players who have dealt with the same injury, including British pair Arthur Fery and Toby Samuel.

Both players endured frustrating long spells on the sidelines, but have each come out of the other side to enjoy the best results of their careers.

Fery, 24, was a shock Wimbledon semi-finalist last month after suffering with bone bruising for most of 2024 and 2025.

Samuel, 23, is close to breaking into the world's top 100 having come back from almost a year out in 2024.

Eventually the pair felt they were able to play through the pain, but Draper remains at the stage of his recovery where he is happy to continue taking extra caution.

"It is a tough injury because there's no set time or magic cure for it," Samuel told BBC Sport.

"At first it was tough to play again. I was still feeling pain and not playing amazing. But I came through it and I haven't looked back."

Since first becoming aware of the problem in May 2025, Draper has taken a series of measures to alleviate the issue.

Initially he tried to play through the discomfort, before withdrawing from last year's US Open before his second-round match and swiftly deciding to curtail his 2025 season.

Draper opted not to play this year's Australian Open in January, then missing the French Open and Wimbledon as he continued to take precautionary moves.

Another tactic saw Draper switch to a platform serve - standing with his feet slightly wider throughout the motion to allow a smoother transfer of weight - which put less load on his arm but "didn't necessarily help" his knee, which he injured at the Barcelona Open in April.

Spending more time in ice baths, saunas and red light therapy has also become an important part of his recovery.

"You start looking into all things when you have this type of injury," Draper said at Wimbledon last month.

"I definitely looked more into my sleep and nutrition. I always did these things pretty well, but it's probably now an elite level.

"I think that will help the longevity of my career hopefully - going through this experience now."

title: Tolchard joy at gold in fifth Commonwealth Games
description: Sam Tolchard says winning his first Commonwealth Games gold medal at his fifth games "means everything".
fullText:
Sam Tolchard says winning his first gold medal at his fifth Commonwealth Games "means everything".

The 37-year-old from Torquay beat Malaysia's Izzat Shameer Dzulkeple to win the men's bowls singles at Glasgow 2026.

Tolchard, who first competed at the Games in Delhi in 2010, cruised to an 8-0 win in the first set.

But he was 6-3 down going into the final two ends of the second set until he picked up a four-shot maximum in the penultimate end to make it 7-6 before earning a one-shot win on a dramatic final end.

"I've had some really hard defeats over the years to take, but I've kept going," said Tolchard, who won silver in the pairs in 2022.

He also has three bronze medals, won in the pairs in 2014 and 2018 and the fours four years ago.

"A fifth Commonwealth Games - a lot of people don't get that many chances," he told BBC Sport. "I'm very fortunate to have had that many chances.

"Once every four years is extremely tough, especially when you're only getting one event like this. We've been fortunate to get two events before.

"Every game I've played now, every bit of practice has been worth it."

Commonwealth Games daily schedule

Commonwealth Games medal table and results

What are the Commonwealth Games?

It is the second time Tolchard has beaten Dzulkeple in a major final. He defeated the Malaysian in the World Champion of Champions event in 2022 for his first major title.

The win in Glasgow is even more remarkable given Tolchard balances playing top-level bowls while working as a self-employed electrician in Devon.

"The week before I came here I was working ridiculously late to try and get jobs finished," he said.

"Being an amateur sport, it's really tough for us, but that is probably what we're used to and that's what hardens us up.

"Hopefully, bowls can just be seen in this light more and more and it can get more and more help. That would be amazing."

Tolchard emulated his sister Sophie, who won gold at the 2014 Commonwealth Games, on an emotional morning for the father-of-one, whose father Ray was a first-class cricket umpire before passing away almost 22 years ago.

"My dad died when I was 15 and he put everything into me," Tolchard said.

"So that's a long time, it'll literally be 22 years on August 1st.

"He put everything into me, and mum as well. I was so fortunate to have that start and I wouldn't be here today without their support."

title: Idi Amin's boxer grandson determined to become new King of Scotland
description: Aziz Abdul wants Ugandans to recognise him as a Commonwealth Games boxing gold medallist rather than as Idi Amin's grandson.
fullText:
Aziz Abdul never met his grandfather. He was a military dictator and died in exile when little Aziz was a toddler. His name was Idi Amin.

Globally, he had another name. The Butcher of Uganda.

Amin took charge of his homeland in a coup in 1971 - becoming the country's third president - and ran a brutal regime for eight years. It's estimated half a million people were killed and the country's entire Asian population were expelled.

He married six times and fathered around 60 children. Or, rather, that's how many he acknowledged. Somewhere among all that, belongs Abdul.

This week, the 25-year-old is one of around 3,000 athletes in Glasgow. Just another face in a tracksuit, here for the Commonwealth Games. But not many others have the lineage that the super-heavyweight boxer does.

Abdul fights England's Damar Thomas in the quarter-finals of the 90+kg category on Wednesday, knowing victory will guarantee at least bronze and make him Uganda's first Commonwealth boxing medallist since Auckland in 1990.

That it could come in Glasgow is particularly pertinent.

The despotic Amin harboured a fascination with Scotland after serving in the King's African Rifles in his 20s. At the height of regime, he was fond of wearing a kilt and playing the bagpipes - and even declared himself "King of Scotland" in 1976.

Some years later, those predilections even spawned an Oscar-winning film, The Last King Of Scotland, starring Forest Whitaker and James McAvoy.

So what would it mean to Abdul - who goes by the nickname Ringo - to win gold in Glasgow?

"In everything we do, God knows tomorrow," he told BBC Sport Scotland. "It's God's plan. I might be the new King of Scotland. It's possible.

"When I arrived, I put up the flag, 'cause I like Scotland so much."

Amin was an accomplished fighter himself, holding the Ugandan light-heavyweight title for nine years from 1951. Even that was not without controversy, though.

Having been beaten in one fight during that time, he reportedly decreed a rematch after taking power, and delivered a staged knockout while wearing his a suit and tie.

In a previous interview, Abdul said he was "inspired" by Amin, although it was not entirely clear whether was was talking about his boxing feats or not.

He refused to answer when asked if he was proud to be the dictator's grandson, but he did address the question of how he feels when he is linked to someone with such a sinister reputation.

"Sometimes people say positive about him, but others say negative about him," he explained. "That's why I don't want to talk more about him.

"It's not good to say something negative about someone who is not there, and it's not good to say something about someone negative who was not there by the time when the incident happened, if it happened."

Idi Amin Part 1: The Butcher of Uganda

As well as those killed under Amin's rule, many more were imprisoned and tortured.

Human rights groups and the Ugandan government both expressed disappointment that he never faced trial for his alleged crimes before dying in Saudi Arabia in 2003.

All this happened long before Abdul was born, clearly. His life in Kampala has been an ordinary one but now he has the chance to make a positive contribution to the reputation of Uganda.

He wants the gold chain he wears around his neck to be replaced with a gold medal this week. He believe his "Ringo punch" will be too much for his rivals.

"Our first medal will be won tomorrow. No excuse," he says. "That's why I'm here. I have that dream that I'm gonna go back with gold medal. That's the reason I'm here in Glasgow right now.

"I want to do something for my country. I think the day is tomorrow for them to recognise me and for the world to recognise me. I want to be known as the Ringo the boxer."

title: World champion Dubois splits with trainer McGuigan
description: British world champion Caroline Dubois has split with trainer Shane McGuigan and will be relocating to America.
fullText:
British world champion Caroline Dubois has split with trainer Shane McGuigan and will be relocating to America.

The unified lightweight champion will defend her WBC and WBO titles against American Amelia Moore on 29 August on an all-female Most Valuable Promotions (MVP) card in Birmingham.

Dubois, 25, confirmed she and McGuigan had mutually agreed to part ways after working together since she turned professional in 2021.

She told BBC Sport: "I had a phenomenal time with Shane. There's been no bitterness, no break-up, no clash, no drift.

"This is the next step I need to help me progress."

Dubois did not reveal the identity of her new trainer, although it is understood she will now work with American coach Manny Robles.

The news emerged just hours before Wednesday's news conference in London, where the British and American fighters gathered to promote the UK v USA-themed event.

The event at BP Pulse Live arena will be headlined by a light-middleweight unification bout between Britain's Chantelle Cameron, 35, and American Mikaela Mayer.

Also on the card, three-weight world champion Terri Harper, 29, returns for the first time since her defeat by Dubois, taking on Texas fighter Miranda Reyes.

Glaziers Hall, overlooking the River Thames, was decorated with banners highlighting each fighter's achievements, showcasing the depth of talent assembled for what is arguably one of the strongest women's boxing cards of the year.

Dubois' exchange with Moore began in light-hearted fashion, with the American joking Britons have "amazing manners", but need to put more salt on their food.

Moore, 36, then gifted Dubois a Los Angeles Lakers cap to "congratulate Caroline on becoming American".

The Londoner smiled throughout the exchange, but the playful moment quickly gave way to the confidence that has become a trademark of her public persona in recent years.

Once known as a quieter figure outside the ring, Dubois has increasingly embraced the spotlight and become one of women's boxing's most outspoken champions.

"I always say I'm on a quest for greatness," she said. "I want to be the best fighter you've ever seen. I want to step into the ring and set the stage alight."

If Dubois gets past Moore, she has targeted further unification fights. The WBA title is currently held by American Stephanie Han, while Turkey's Elif Nur Turhan holds the IBF belt.

Dubois also reiterated a fight with American Alycia Baumgardner remains high on her wishlist, but claimed her 32-year-old rival has shown little interest in making the bout happen

Cameron, who regained a world title in April by beating Michaela Kotaskova for the vacant WBO belt, is aiming to add 36-year-old Mayer's WBC and WBA titles to her collection.

"I'm a different breed. The tougher my challenge, the better I am," said the 35-year-old from Northampton.

The pair - who first met as amateurs and kept in touch - struck a respectful tone throughout the media-only event, with both stressing the importance of elite fighters facing one another.

"Hopefully for women's boxing, more fights like this happen. The best fight the best," added Cameron. "Stop talking and make the fights happen."

Mayer, preparing for her fifth fight in Britain, said their contest would "grow and develop women's boxing".

Earlier in the day, MVP announced a new partnership with Matchroom Boxing designed to create more opportunities for female fighters across both promotional rosters.

The agreement is expected to create more crossover opportunities, allowing fighters from both promotions to compete on each other's cards.

The promotion also unveiled Australian two-weight world champion Skye Nicolson as a surprise new signing after her departure from Matchroom.

The 30-year-old will make her MVP debut on the Birmingham card, where she is set to defend her WBC super-bantamweight title against Miyo Yoshida.

"I've always wanted to be in the big fights and I feel this is the place to make the big fights happen," said Nicolson.

fullText:
Chelsea are set to sign attacking midfielder Giulia Dragoni from Barcelona.

The 19-year-old spent the last two seasons on loan at Roma, and Chelsea have been tracking her progress for several years.

Dragoni has already made 24 appearances for Italy since her debut aged 16 and has experience in the Women’s Champions League with Roma.

She joined Barcelona in 2023 after graduating from Inter Milan’s youth academy.

It is understood Chelsea were attracted to Dragoni's quality because of her versatility and ability to play across multiple attacking positions and in midfield.

title: Classy Mandhana helps Super Giants beat Sunrisers
description: Smriti Mandhana's masterful unbeaten 88 off 50 balls guides Manchester Super Giants to a four-wicket win over Sunrisers Leeds in The Hundred.
fullText:
The Hundred women's competition, Headingley

Sunrisers Leeds 142-4 (100 balls): Sutherland 35 (24); Villiers 1-6

Manchester Super Giants 147-6 (96 balls): Mandhana 88* (50); Baker 1-9

Manchester Super Giants won by four wickets

Smriti Mandhana made a masterful unbeaten 88 off 50 balls as she guided Manchester Super Giants to a four-wicket win over Sunrisers Leeds which maintained their unbeaten start to The Hundred.

The India opener's sixth half-century in the history of the tournament was her top score and included seven fours and four sixes.

Mandhana's unflappable temperament at Headingley was the key as as the stylish left-hander skilfully paced a chase of 143 despite wickets falling around her.

It was a testament to the quality of the knock that Super Giants skipper Meg Lanning, who made 24, was the only other player into double figures.

Mandhana said the key to her innings was "just committing to the shot" and "not playing anything half-heartedly".

"If you win matches like this, it really puts us in a good place," she told Sky Sports.

"In franchise cricket, you have to keep your head down and keep going taking the good days with bad days."

Mandhana had kept the Super Giants in touch with the run rate throughout their reply before she went for the jugular with 16 needed off the last 10 balls.

The 30-year-old slog-swept Jess Jonassen for six - Darcey Carter allowing the ball to go through her grasp at deep mid-wicket - before pumping the Aussie spinner down the ground and over the ropes again.

Mandhana then sealed the win in style off the first ball of the final set when she dispatched Annabel Sutherland back over her head for six.

Earlier, Sutherland had top scored for Sunrisers with a controlled 35 off 24 balls, striking four fours, in their total of 142-4.

Bryony Smith and Phoebe Litchfield also chipped in with 26 and 31 respectively while Dani Gibson gave the innings late impetus as she clubbed 18 off just six balls.

Grace Ballinger was the most economical of the Super Giants bowlers as her 20 wicketless balls cost only 17 runs.

However, spinner Sophie Ecclestone had a rare off day as her allocation went for 30, while fellow England international Ryana MacDonald-Gay went for six runs more.

The Hundred continues on Wednesday with double-headers in Cardiff and London.

At Sophia Gardens, Welsh Fire's women face Trent Rockets at 11:30 BST before the men's sides meet at 15:00 BST, with both home teams aiming to build on positive starts to the campaign.

Meanwhile, it is derby day at The Oval, MI London's women take on London Spirit at 15:00 BST before the men's fixture gets under way at 18:30 BST, as both sides look to gain early momentum in the race for the knockout stages.
